review_notes: I read the whole file. I also grepped the Construction directory for the same Fin.cases/Fin.addCases pattern. It appears 64 times across 26 files, including the equivalence proof in InitialSpectatorSplit.lean. I found no existing shared induction principle for the 1+b+(d+r) index layout. The other proofs here are not repeated machinery: the product, identity, bound and budget lemmas are each used once and share only short calculations. The proposed lemma has not been compiled, and the exact casts of the Fin index terms in its statement would need checking. The finding is modest because the repeated reasoning is structural case-splitting, not deep mathematics.

findings.problem: Both theorems prove a pointwise property of the layout `Fin.cons _ (Fin.append _ (Fin.append _ _))` with the same four-way decomposition. They split with `Fin.cases`, then `Fin.addCases`, then a nested `Fin.addCases`. Each of the four leaves is closed by a `simpa only [initialHalfNormalizer, Fin.cons_succ, Fin.append_left/right]` call that differs only in which simp lemmas fire. The index-decomposition proof is therefore written twice. The same split recurs in at least 26 files in this directory, for example `Fin.addCases` in the `right_inv` proof of `InitialSpectatorSplit.lean`.
findings.proposed_change: Prove one induction principle for this layout. Sketch: `theorem forall_initial_layout {b d r : ℕ} {Q : Fin ((b + (d + r)) + 1) → Prop} (h0 : Q 0) (hb : ∀ j : Fin b, Q (j.castAdd (d + r)).succ) (hd : ∀ t : Fin d, Q ((t.castAdd r).natAdd b).succ) (hc : ∀ t : Fin r, Q ((t.natAdd d).natAdd b).succ) : ∀ i, Q i`. Prove it once by `Fin.cases` followed by two `Fin.addCases`. Add simp lemmas for the four values of `initialHalfNormalizer`: at `0`, and at the three `succ`/`castAdd`/`natAdd` positions. Then `initialHalfNormalizer_nonneg` becomes `forall_initial_layout` applied to four one-line goals (`Real.exp_nonneg _`, then `inv_nonneg.mpr (mul_nonneg ha hL)` twice, then `Real.exp_nonneg _`). `initialHalfNormalizer_prime_bound` becomes `forall_initial_layout` applied to `h₀ q`, `hb _ q`, `hd _ q` and `hc _ q`, after rewriting with the value simp lemmas. The same lemma could replace the repeated splits in the sibling files.
findings.benefit: The layout-splitting argument is stated and maintained once. Each of the two theorems shrinks to its four mathematical leaves instead of nested `refine`/`simpa only` blocks with hand-picked simp sets. A change to the slot layout, such as reordering the blocks, would then need one edit, not edits in every proof that does this split.
